build.notes:
How the app's UI thread uses this (native/core/qrss/em_api.hpp):

1. Never call refine/retro on the GUI thread: each blocks its caller until done. Per unit of work (measured RelWithDebInfo, one core of a shared 4-CPU box): refine per pass re-received TINY ~0.1 s, SHORT 0.3-1.2 s, FULL 3-5 s, times rounds (default 3, stopping early once a round gains < 0.05 dB); retro per slot searched TINY ~0.2 s, SHORT ~0.9 s, FULL ~6 s plus a receive per find; a full 48 h passband store (192 slots) is ~3 min SHORT, ~20 min FULL. Run them on a worker (std::thread / QThreadPool / QtConcurrent).
2. Before enabling the buttons (cheap, any thread): em_api::check_picture(store, key); for "search the recording" also retro_frame(name) and, without a session, check_passband_dir(dir). Catch em_api::Refusal (NoPicture, NoPassbandStore, NotCeFrame, UnknownFrame) and show e.what() -- the CLI's texts. std::invalid_argument means a bad estimator name.
3. Sharing with the in-process listener: with a listen_api::Session running, pass its own objects -- refine(*session->store(), key, opts, hooks) and retro(*session->store(), key, Passband::of(session->passband()), "short", {}, hooks). Copy the shared_ptrs into the worker lambda; they stay valid after the session ends. No dir lock is taken (as qrss_decode.py), so a second store::Store(root) also works when there is no session. A pass the listener attaches meanwhile is re-received from the next round; progress total grows to include it.
4. Progress: em::Hooks.progress(done, total, what) runs on the worker thread with no lock held; marshal it (QMetaObject::invokeMethod with Qt::QueuedConnection) to a QProgressBar: done rises by one per pass/slot, total never falls except refine's final (done, done, "converged after round r") which closes the bar early. hooks.log gives the reference's text lines for a log pane.
5. Cancel: own a std::atomic<bool> in the UI object (outliving the worker), set hooks.cancel = &flag, wire the Cancel button to flag = true. The call returns (never throws Cancelled) with result.cancelled = true within one re-receive's tracker run (refine) or one (segment, candidate) search (retro); every pass listed in RefineResult.passes / RetroResult.finds is stored and its accumulator rebuilt, the one in flight is not. Reset the flag before the next call.
6. Results: RefineResult.history (mean W before and after each round), .passes (round, uid, mean W before/after each), .mean_w_db; RetroResult.finds (q, f_hz, Z, segment, key, rule, uid, mean W), slots_total/done/searched. Then re-read store.accumulator(key) on the worker, render with the codec, and post the picture to the GUI thread.
7. Receiver rules (QRSS_OLD_EDGE_NOISE) are process environment: set once at startup (rules::apply), never per call.
